title: AAPS continuously attempts to connect to Omnipod after deactivating
body: Reporting this issue still exists: https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/issues/4542 A14, AAPS 3.4.2.2. AAPS continuously tries to connect to a pod after deactivating an active pod.

comments.body:
Also same stays 0/0 :0% connecting for xxx s.  Don't know if it is trying or the counter is just running.  After new active pod visit to Dash tab shows constant (seconds not counting) 0/0:: 0% Connecting for 123 s (I think no picture) although populated with priming amount etc.  Didn't try refresh but made bolus and returned and seemed to be working.
Samsung A55, Android 14, UI 6.1, AAPS 3.4.2.2.

Agree, the issue is not fixed yet.

There seems to be some ambiguity in the `Pump.kt` interface around the semantics of `isInitialized()`, `isConnected()` and `isBusy()`. At least their semantics seems to differ across drivers (e.g. Dana, Dash, and Medtrum), so it’s not entirely clear what the intended contract is.

My current understanding is that `isBusy()` returns `true` when activationProgress is `NOT_STARTED`. This prevents the exit conditions in `QueueWorker` from ever firing, resulting in an infinite loop (as `isConnected()` also returns `true`). Excluding `NOT_STARTED` from the “busy” range would resolve this issue. However, given the ambiguity in the interface semantics, I don’t think this is a straightforward change and it probably deserves a more thorough review.

If my understanding is correct, the fix would be in `OmnipodDashPumpPlugin.kt`:

```kotlin
override fun isBusy(): Boolean {
    // prevents the queue from executing commands
    return podStateManager.activationProgress != ActivationProgress.NOT_STARTED &&
        podStateManager.activationProgress.isBefore(ActivationProgress.COMPLETED)
}
```

The fix resolves the issue - will promote it to PR
